checks.check: residue 1 at the origin for all four kernels
the odd kernel is doubly periodic and odd, and vanishes at the three marks
at tau = i the odd kernel is zeta(z) - pi conj(z): the holomorphic part has no linear term, G2*(i) = 0
the two even kernels exchanged by the symmetry are pulled back to the third one: 2 -> 3 and 4 -> 3
the third even kernel is pulled back into the odd structure: alpha S3(alpha z) = Z(z) - Z(z + c)
the odd kernel is self-similar under the step: alpha Z(alpha z) = Z(z) + Z(z + c)
the purely holomorphic zeta is not self-similar; the term -pi conj(z) is needed
control: at a generic torus the odd kernel obeys the same law under the integer 2 (so integers are not special to tau = i)
control: at a generic torus 1+i is no map of the torus (the image of the lattice leaves the lattice)
round sphere: the pulled back kernel is the kernel times sqrt((1+x^2)(1+y^2))/(1+xy), not the kernel
its defect: a second pole on the other sheet (y = -1/x) and branch points at the critical points +-i

verdict.even_torus_kernels: not self-similar; the step moves them 2,4 -> 3 -> odd, as it moves the marks
verdict.odd_kernel: self-similar under every Gaussian integer; Z(z) = zeta(z) - pi conj(z)
